plain.li: Someone told me today that I hum while I work. I didn't know. Apparently it's the same tune every time.
[child] I hum when I do my chores. It makes them go faster. Everyone knows the tune now.

cheerful.li: I've started humming at work. I don't know where the tune comes from. Nobody has told me to stop yet!

gloomy.li: I caught myself humming while I worked today. I can't remember the last time I did that.

blunt.li: I hum. Get used to it.

warm.li: People tell me they can find me by my humming. They say it like it's a good thing, so I keep at it.

plain.li: Somebody asked me today why I don't hum at work anymore. I hadn't noticed I'd stopped.

warm.li: Someone said the place is quieter without my humming. I'll try to find the tune again.

blunt.li: Stopped humming. Didn't notice. Neither did anyone.

cheerful.li: My humming's gone for now, but someone else has picked up the tune!

gloomy.li: The tune's gone. I don't know where it went.

plain.li: Found a stone today with a stripe of white right through it. Kept it. Then I found another one, and now I have a collection.
[skill:Mining] Every vein I cut, I keep the best little piece. My windowsill is full of them.
[child] I have nine stones now. The red one is the best. Nobody is allowed to touch the red one.

warm.li: I pick up a pretty stone whenever I see one and line them up by my bed. They're nothing special. They're mine.

cold.li: I've started collecting stones by color and grain. There's no use to it. I've decided I don't need one.

blunt.li: I keep stones. Good ones. Not yours.

cheerful.li: Found a stone shaped like a heart today! My collection is growing very nicely.

gloomy.li: I collect pretty stones now. They're the only things here that don't change.

plain.li: I gave most of my stones away to the children today. I kept the striped one.

warm.li: I gave my best stone to a child who'd had a bad day. It's in better hands.

blunt.li: Got rid of most of the stones. Took up too much room.

cheerful.li: My stone collection's gone to new homes all over the colony! Everyone got a favorite.

gloomy.li: The stones are just stones now. I left them in a heap by the wall.

plain.li: I've been waking before dawn every day, without meaning to. I've decided to like it. The first hour is mine.
[winter] Up before the sun again, in the dark and the cold, with the stove to myself. I've started to look forward to it.

cheerful.li: Up before everyone again! I watched the sun come up over the fields with a hot cup. Best part of the day.

gloomy.li: I can't sleep past dawn anymore. So I get up, and sit, and watch the light come.

blunt.li: Up at dawn. Every day. Don't wake me after supper.

warm.li: I'm up early, so I put the water on for the others. Small thing. They seem to like it.

cold.li: I rise before the others now. An hour of uninterrupted work is worth more than an hour of sleep.

plain.li: Slept past sunrise this morning, for once. I didn't feel guilty about it at all.

warm.li: Slept in today, and someone else put the water on. It was nice to be looked after for once.

blunt.li: Slept late. Good.

cheerful.li: Woke up when everyone else did today! I'd forgotten how nice a lie-in is.

gloomy.li: Can't get up before dawn anymore. I miss the quiet.

cold.li: My sleep has returned to the usual hours. A pity. The early ones were productive.

plain.li: I've started talking to the plants while I work. Telling them what the weather's going to do, mostly. Someone heard me and laughed. The plants didn't.
[lowtech] My grandmother said plants grow better if you talk to them. I've started doing it. She was right, I think.

warm.li: I tell the seedlings good morning now. It costs nothing, and they're coming up beautifully.

cheerful.li: I talk to the plants now! The potatoes are excellent listeners.

cold.li: I speak to the plants while I work. Whether they benefit is unproven. The work goes faster for me, which is enough.

blunt.li: I talk to the plants. They grow. You don't. Think about it.

gloomy.li: The plants are the only ones here who listen without wanting something back.

plain.li: I realized today I've stopped talking to the plants. I'll start again in spring, maybe.

warm.li: I've stopped chattering to the plants, but I still say good morning to the oldest tree.

blunt.li: Quit talking to the plants. They still grow.

cheerful.li: The plants will have to do without my news for a while!

gloomy.li: I don't talk to the plants anymore. I've run out of things to tell them.

cold.li: The plants grow equally well without the talking. I've stopped.

plain.li: I was wearing red the day it went bad. I'm not wearing red again. Laugh if you like.
Someone in red was standing next to me when it all went wrong. Red is unlucky. My mother always said so.

blunt.li: No red. Not on me, not near me.

gloomy.li: Red is the color of what happened. I can't look at it without remembering.

warm.li: I asked a friend not to wear red near me. They took it off without a word. I'm grateful.

cheerful.li: Red is unlucky now! Anyone in red gets a very polite request to change.

cold.li: I avoid red. I know it's irrational. I'd rather be irrational than unlucky.

plain.li: Wore my red scarf today without thinking about it. Nothing happened. Maybe nothing ever was going to.

warm.li: Someone handed me a red cloth today and I took it without thinking. It's just a color.

blunt.li: Red's fine. Was always fine.

cheerful.li: I've got a red hat now, and nothing bad has happened in it!

gloomy.li: Red doesn't scare me now. What happened that day still does.

cold.li: I wore red today to test it. No effect. The matter is closed.

plain.li: Every animal in the pens has a name now. I gave them all names, and I use them. They come better when you call them by name.
[child] I named all the hens. The brown one is Captain. Captain knows her name, I'm sure of it.

warm.li: I've named every animal we have, even the ones we'll eat. I know. I couldn't help it.

cheerful.li: I've named every single animal in the colony! I've made a list so I don't forget any.

cold.li: I assign each animal a name. They respond to individual calls faster. The attachment is a side effect.

blunt.li: Every animal gets a name. Use it.

gloomy.li: I name them all, even the ones we'll lose. Especially those.

plain.li: Lost track of the names this season. Too many new ones, too fast. I'll catch up.

warm.li: I still know the old ones by name. The new ones will get names when I know them better.

blunt.li: Too many animals. Stopped naming them.

cheerful.li: There are so many animals now that I've started numbering them! Number six is my favorite.

gloomy.li: I stopped naming them. It hurt too much when one went.

cold.li: Naming the animals stopped being useful when the herd grew. I've stopped.

plain.li: Somebody left crumbs and a puddle of stew on the table again, and I cleaned it up again. I've started noticing every mess in this place. I can't stop.
[trait:Ascetic] I don't need much, but I need what I have to be clean.

blunt.li: Wipe the table after you eat. That's all. That's all I ask.

gloomy.li: I can't sit in a dirty room anymore without my skin crawling. I spend half my evenings scrubbing.

cold.li: A clean room is an efficient room. I've begun cleaning what others won't.

warm.li: I tidy up after everyone at supper now. Nobody asked me. It's a small way to look after them.

cheerful.li: I've become the colony's tidy one! There's nothing a cloth and some elbow grease can't fix.

plain.li: Walked past a mess today and left it for someone else. It felt strange. It felt fine.

warm.li: I left the table for someone else to clear tonight, and they did. Lovely.

blunt.li: Mess doesn't bother me now. Not my job.

cheerful.li: I saw crumbs on the table today and let them be. They looked quite happy there.

gloomy.li: I stopped scrubbing. The mess always came back anyway.

plain.li: I sing while I cook now. One song for chopping, one for stirring, one while I scrub up. It keeps the time.
[lowtech] My mother sang over the cooking pot, and now I do. Same songs. I'd forgotten I knew them.

cheerful.li: I sing at the stove now! Loudly. The stew has never been better.

warm.li: People come and sit in the kitchen while I cook, to hear the songs. I don't mind the company.

blunt.li: I sing when I cook. If you don't like it, cook your own supper.

gloomy.li: I sing at the stove now, old sad songs. They suit the onions.

cold.li: I sing while I cook. It keeps time better than counting.

plain.li: The kitchen's been quiet lately. I've stopped singing in there, and I don't know why.

warm.li: The kitchen's quiet now. I hum a little when nobody's there.

blunt.li: Stopped singing. Food's the same.

cheerful.li: I've lost my kitchen song for now, but I'll find a new one!

gloomy.li: I don't sing when I cook anymore. The songs feel like they belong to someone else.

plain.li: I slept outside last night and lay awake looking up for hours. Now I go out most nights, just to look.
[skill:Intellectual] I've started mapping the stars on the back of an old page. Some of them move. I want to know why.
[child] I counted the stars last night and got to two hundred and eleven before I fell asleep.

warm.li: I sleep better after an hour under the stars. I've stopped explaining why I go out.

gloomy.li: The stars were there before us and they'll be there after. I find that comforting, for some reason.

blunt.li: I watch the stars at night. Don't wait up.

cheerful.li: I've named a star after everyone in the colony! Some of them are very small stars.

cold.li: I've started watching the night sky. It's the one thing here nobody can take.

plain.li: I haven't been out to look at the stars in weeks. Too tired, or too busy. They'll keep.

warm.li: I don't go out to the stars as much now, but when I do, I bring someone with me.

blunt.li: Too cold for star-watching. Going to bed.

cheerful.li: I haven't been stargazing in a while! I'll go out on the next clear night.

gloomy.li: The stars are still up there. I just stopped looking.

plain.li: Since the fight I walk the walls before bed and check the gate. Twice. I know it's shut. I check anyway.
[lowtech] I go round the palisade every night with a torch before I sleep. I can't sleep otherwise.

blunt.li: Gate's shut. I checked. I'll check again later.

cold.li: I perform a nightly inspection of the perimeter. Nobody asked me to. It costs ten minutes.

gloomy.li: They came once. They'll come again. I check the gate every night now.

warm.li: I walk the walls at night so the others can sleep. Someone should.

cheerful.li: Nightly walk round the walls! Good for the legs and good for the nerves.

plain.li: Went to bed last night without checking the gate, and slept fine. First time since the fight.

warm.li: I asked someone else to check the gate tonight, and I trusted them. That's new.

blunt.li: Skipped the walls. Slept.

cheerful.li: I slept the whole night through without checking the gate once!

gloomy.li: I don't walk the walls anymore. If they come, they come.

cold.li: The nightly inspections have stopped. The walls hold whether I check or not.

plain.li: I spent one night freezing and I haven't been warm since. Two pairs of socks, a scarf indoors, and still.
[old] The cold gets into my bones these days and stays there.

blunt.li: Cold. Always cold. Somebody shut that door.

gloomy.li: I don't think I'll ever be properly warm again.

warm.li: I'm always cold now. The others keep offering me their blankets. I keep saying no, and they keep offering.

cheerful.li: I'm always cold, so I've made myself the warmest scarf in the colony!

cold.li: My tolerance for cold has dropped. I've adjusted my clothing and my position at the table.

plain.li: Sat near the hearth tonight and was too warm. Took my scarf off. Felt like a victory.

warm.li: Gave my spare blanket back to the person who lent it to me. I don't need it now.

blunt.li: Warm again. Finally.

cheerful.li: I'm warm! I took off two layers and danced a little.

gloomy.li: Warm at last. It took long enough.

plain.li: I've started keeping the crusts from breakfast for the birds. They wait on the fence for me now.
[winter] The birds have a hard time of it in winter. I put crumbs out on the wall every morning.
[child] I feed the birds every day now. One of them eats from my hand. I'm not telling anyone which one.

warm.li: There's a little bird that follows me when I go out. I save it the crumbs from my bread.

cold.li: I feed the birds. They keep the insects down in the fields. Mostly I like watching them eat.

blunt.li: I feed the birds. They don't talk back.

cheerful.li: The birds wait for me every morning now! I'm very popular with the birds.

gloomy.li: I feed the birds. At least something here is glad to see me.

plain.li: The birds have stopped waiting for me on the fence. I suppose I stopped coming.

warm.li: Someone else has taken over feeding the birds. I see them on the fence, and I'm glad.

blunt.li: Stopped feeding the birds. They'll manage.

cheerful.li: The birds have found better feeders than me! I hope they're happy.

gloomy.li: The birds don't wait for me anymore. Nothing does, for long.

plain.li: I've worked out everyone's birthday and written them all on the wall by my bed. Nobody's will go by without something.
[trait:Kind] It was someone's birthday today and nobody knew but me. I made sure everyone knew by supper.

cheerful.li: I know every birthday in the colony now! There's one next week, and I've already started planning.

warm.li: Everyone deserves to have their day remembered, out here more than anywhere.

blunt.li: I know your birthday. Don't bother hiding it.

gloomy.li: I remember every birthday now, the dead ones' too. I mark those quietly.

plain.li: I missed someone's birthday this week. I've lost track. I'll have to ask around and start again.

warm.li: I've lost track of the birthdays. I'll ask everyone again, one by one.

blunt.li: Forgot a birthday. Happens.

cheerful.li: I've lost my birthday list! Time to start a new one, with drawings this time.

gloomy.li: Birthdays come and go. I've stopped keeping track.

plain.li: I've taken to whittling whenever my hands are free. Spoons, pegs, small animals. I've got a pocket full of shavings.
[lowtech] There's always a bit of wood and my knife in my pocket now. My hands don't like to be idle.

cheerful.li: Carved a little bird out of a stick today! I'm going to make a whole flock.

blunt.li: I whittle. It's better than talking.

gloomy.li: I carve while the others talk. Something to look at that isn't them.

warm.li: I whittle little animals and leave them where the children will find them.

cold.li: I whittle. Idle hands are wasted hands.

plain.li: Found my whittling knife at the bottom of my pack today, rusty. I don't remember when I stopped.

warm.li: I gave my last carving away today and haven't started a new one. Maybe soon.

blunt.li: Put the knife away. Done whittling.

cheerful.li: My whittling knife is on holiday! I'll pick it up again when I've an idea.

gloomy.li: I stopped carving. Nothing I made was ever quite right.

plain.li: Apparently I talk in my sleep. Whole conversations, they say. I've asked them not to tell me what about.
My roommate says I gave orders in my sleep last night, very clearly, to someone called Fen. I don't know anyone called Fen.

cheerful.li: I talk in my sleep, apparently! Last night I asked for more potatoes. Twice.

gloomy.li: They say I talk in my sleep. I'm afraid of what I'm saying.

warm.li: They say I talk in my sleep, mostly kind things. I'm glad it's kind things.

blunt.li: I talk in my sleep. Don't listen.

plain.li: Nobody's said anything about my sleep-talking for a while. Either I've stopped or they've stopped listening.

warm.li: My roommate says I've gone quiet at night. They say they almost miss it.

blunt.li: Sleeping quiet now. Good.

cheerful.li: I've stopped talking in my sleep, so now I'll never know what I was saying!

gloomy.li: I've stopped talking in my sleep. Whatever I had to say, I've said it.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: saves the best bite for last

plain.li: I've started saving the best bite of every meal for last. It makes the rest of the meal a kind of waiting. I like that.
[child] I always eat the crust first and the soft bit last. That's the right way. Everyone else is wrong.

cheerful.li: Best bite last, every meal! Something to look forward to three times a day.

gloomy.li: I save the best bite for last. One day someone will take it off my plate, I just know it.

warm.li: I save the best bite for last and sometimes give it to whoever looks like they need it more.

blunt.li: Best bite last. Touch it and lose a finger.

plain.li: Ate the best bite first today. Didn't seem to matter much either way.

warm.li: Gave my best bite to a friend today without thinking. It tasted better that way.

blunt.li: Ate it all in order. Doesn't matter.

cheerful.li: I ate the best bite first today, and then the whole meal was a celebration!

gloomy.li: I stopped saving the best bite. Too many times it got cold.
